title: Distinct Distances in General Position: n/2 Lower Bound

problemStatement.formal: ∀ S : Finset Point2D, inGeneralPosition S → (distinctDistances S).card ≥ S.card / 2
problemStatement.plain: Does every set of n points in general position (no 3 collinear) in ℝ² determine at least ⌊n/2⌋ distinct distances?
whyMatters: Strengthens Szemerédi's proved n/3 bound for general position
Related to the famous Erdős distinct distances problem (#89)
The stronger per-point version (Conjecture 2) is disproved, but the total distance version remains open

proven: Szemerédi: n/3 distinct distances in general position (unpublished ~1975)
Guth-Katz: Ω(n/log n) distinct distances for any point set (2015)
Conjecture 2 (per-point n/2) disproved by Xichuan's 42-point counterexample
Distance function properties: symmetry, non-negativity, positive-definiteness (proved in Lean)
Collinearity invariance under cyclic permutation and transposition (proved in Lean)
General position is hereditary under subsets (proved in Lean)
open: Conjecture 1: Does general position guarantee ≥ n/2 total distinct distances?
What is the best constant c such that general position guarantees ≥ cn distinct distances?
knownResults.goal: Formalize the known results and structural relationships around the open conjecture

currentState.focus: Improved formalization with proved infrastructure theorems
blockers: Conjecture 1 is an OPEN problem - cannot be proved
currentState.nextAction: Submit to Aristotle for potential improvement of axiom proofs

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Improved Erdos1082Problem.lean from 4 proved theorems/7 axioms to 20 proved theorems/4 axioms/0 sorries. Removed 2 placeholder True axioms. Proved C2→C1 implication, distance metric properties, collinearity symmetry, general position heredity, and distance subset relationships.
insights: Conjecture 1 (total distances ≥ n/2) and Conjecture 2 (per-point ≥ n/2) are independent: C2→C1 but ¬C2 does not give ¬C1
Xichuan's counterexample (42 points, each with only 20 distances) disproves C2 but could still be consistent with C1
The gap between Szemerédi's n/3 bound and the conjectured n/2 is the key open territory
Using squared distance (distSq) avoids sqrt complications while preserving distinct distance counting
Collinearity via cross-product formula is computationally efficient for Lean formalization
General position (no 3 collinear) is strictly weaker than convex position
builtItems: 8 distance infrastructure theorems (symmetry, non-neg, positive-definiteness, self-distance)
mathlibGaps: No Mathlib formalization of Szemerédi's n/3 bound for general position
No Mathlib infrastructure for Guth-Katz distinct distances result
No Mathlib formalization of collinearity and general position for finite point sets
nextSteps: Submit to Aristotle - some axioms (especially szemeredi_n_over_3) might have Mathlib proofs
Explore whether Guth-Katz Ω(n/log n) can be connected to give n/2 for moderate n
Investigate whether a computational approach could verify C1 for small n
